page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or a GPU, and operates on the Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2055.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 33.32 GB/sec. Text processing and single-threaded bzip3 decompression also rank in the top 25% of tested servers. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a Passmark CPU score of 12373.16 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7957.0. Memory performance represents a notable tradeoff; while cached small-block memory read bandwidth is high at 684.22 GB/sec, the Passmark memory score falls into the bottom 25%, and large-block uncached read and write speeds are 52.11 GB/sec and 50.44 GB/sec respectively.

This server is designed for compute-intensive workloads that benefit from high single-core performance and advanced vector or matrix instructions, such as web serving, software compilation, and lightweight machine learning inference. It achieves 10.68 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 14.29 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Given its compute-to-memory ratio of 1:2 and lack of local storage, it offers a cost-efficient profile for processing-heavy tasks that do not require massive memory footprints or high-speed local disk access.
